verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will reach speeds of approximately 17,000 mph (27,000 km/h) to enter Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the rocket goes soaring off into space at approximately 17,000 mph.'; R4: 'the rocket goes soaring off into space at approximately 17,000 mph.'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for ~17,000 mph speed to enter space/orbit during launch phase.

verifications.claim: During the Artemis II mission's return from the Moon, the Orion capsule will hit a peak reentry speed of over 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '25,000 mph: Speed during Earth reentry'; R3: 'peak reentry speed will be slightly over 25,000 mph (40,200 km/h)'; R5: 'travelling around seven miles a second' (~25,200 mph); R7: '40,000 kilometers per hour (25,000 miles per hour)'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm peak reentry speed over/around 25,000 mph.

verifications.claim: During the Artemis II mission's return from the Moon, the Orion capsule will hit a peak reentry speed of roughly 32 times the speed of sound.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'It's going to hit the Earth's atmosphere at 32 times the speed of sound.'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement matching the exact multiplier for reentry speed.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule reentry is one of the fastest human-rated reentries.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the Orion capsule will reach speeds greater than any other crewed spacecraft in history as it reenters Earth's atmosphere.'
verifications.reasoning: Source explicitly states it will be the fastest crewed reentry.

verifications.claim: During initial launch, the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket accelerates to over 3,100 mph within the first two minutes.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention specific speed of over 3,100 mph in first two minutes.

verifications.claim: During orbit injection, the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket hits around 17,000 mph to reach orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the rocket goes soaring off into space at approximately 17,000 mph.'; R4: same phrasing.
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state ~17,000 mph for SLS rocket entering space/orbit, closely matching orbit injection context.

verifications.claim: During trans-lunar injection, further burns increase the speed to over 22,000 mph to escape Earth's gravity.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'At a rocket’s blistering speed of up to 22,000 miles per hour'
verifications.reasoning: R1 mentions up to 22,000 mph post-launch in debris context, but not explicitly tied to TLI burn.

verifications.claim: During reentry, the Orion capsule hits the atmosphere at 25,000 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '25,000 mph: Speed during Earth reentry'; R3: 'slightly over 25,000 mph'; R7: '25,000 miles per hour'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple direct confirmations of 25,000 mph atmospheric entry speed.

verifications.claim: During reentry, the Orion capsule generates temperatures near 5,000°F.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R7: 'temperatures of about 1,650 degrees Celsius (3,000 degrees Fahrenheit)'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will technically become the fastest-traveling humans in history upon their return.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the Artemis II astronauts will travel faster than any other humans in history (as reentry is the fastest part of any space mission)'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement confirming fastest humans via reentry speed.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will surpass the speeds of Apollo 10 upon their return.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'which would beat the reentry record currently held by the Apollo 10 astronauts'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states surpassing Apollo 10 reentry record.
